text:
maria: heads-up — seeing a 429 spike from hosted API starting ~10:05. billing logs show a lot of requests with project_id=null. looks like 'projectless' API keys are being routed through the generic path.
aj: can you paste an example log line?
maria: sure — from aggregator: `2026-03-18T10:06:12Z level=warn route=generate status=429 tokens=123 origin=service-key id=sk_live_*** project_id=null org_id=org_987`
ravi: ah, so requests still authenticate but we lose project attribution. are those service keys bound to orgs but not projects?
maria: yes — customers can create org-scoped service keys that don't tie to a project, we previously treated them as 'org-default' in UI but not in routing.
dina: caution — auto-assigning a fallback project for billing could be surprising. some orgs expect usage to be 'unattributed' until they migrate. also impersonation surface if we pick wrong project.
kevin: agree on caution. maybe implement sticky routing that maps the first observed project for a key -> prefers that project on subsequent requests. for keys with no observed project, we can surface a console prompt to set a preferred project.
aj: sticky routing sounds good. what's the telemetry we need to validate?
kevin: track `attribution_confidence` per key: values {"explicit_project", "sticky_assigned", "unattributed"}. emit a gauge per-minute and count tokens by category. add a log tag `attrib_hint=sticky` when assigned.
ops-bot: incident alert — generated: 429-rate > 5% for hosted-api across us-west-1 (10:07) :rotating_light:
maria: proposal for mitigation + rollout: 1) add canary feature flag `project_attrib_v2` in console (default off) 2) implement sticky assignment in router when flag on 3) expose console UI to show `Preferred project` for a key and a CTA to change 4) telemetry: metrics `tokens_unattributed`, `tokens_sticky_assigned`, `tokens_explicit` + histogram for `attribution_latency` 5) alert if `tokens_unattributed / tokens_total > 1%` post-rollout
ravi: how do we seed sticky assignments for existing keys? backfill from billing joins? might need a short window to avoid churn.
kevin: backfill plan: run a daily job that scans last 90 days to pick high-confidence project per key (>=80% of tokens from single project). mark those as `sticky_assigned` with source=backfill. keys without confidence remain `unattributed`.
dina: console UX: show a small badge "Unattributed usage: X tokens" on keys without sticky project and a one-click "Select preferred project" flow. make the default non-destructive — only used for billing attribution, not access control. docs must be clear.
aj: one more: telemetry must include `attribution_pulses` to detect oscillation (key switching projects rapidly). add a counter per key for sticky reassigns.
maria: agree. dev plan: small router change + config flag + metrics + console change. roll canary to 5% orgs for 48h, watch `tokens_unattributed` and `billing_join_conflict` logs.
kevin: also add a quick circuit: if request contains explicit `x-project-id` header or project claim in token, always prefer explicit. sticky only used when missing.
ravi: threading with billing: need a join key. billing team: when sticky_assigned=true, they should use that project for invoicing and mark on invoice metadata.
dina: legal & security: ensure audit logs record that attribution was inferred/backfilled. add audit event `project_attribution_changed` with actor=system/backfill/admin.
maria: i'd like a small A/B: half of canary orgs see a console banner prompting to pick a project; half get silent sticky assignment — to measure user confusion vs automatic reduction in unattributed tokens.
aj: timeline?
maria: I'll open a single RFC ticket today. aim for dev + infra changes in 3 days, canary config the following week. I'll add owners: maria (prod), kevin (router), ravi (billing join), dina (console & legal).
ops-bot: created issue #INF-4821: "project attribution sticky routing canary" assigned to maria.
maria: thanks — looping in billing and support for comms. :thumbsup:
aj: :+1:
kevin: will start metric names + prom rules. posting draft alert rule here in thread:
```
alert: HighUnattributedTokens
expr: sum(rate(api_tokens_total{env=\"prod\",attrib_status=\"unattributed\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(api_tokens_total{env=\"prod\"}[5m])) > 0.01
for: 15m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Unattributed tokens >1%"
  runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/attrib
```
maria: perfect. i'll file the RFC and call a 20-min sync once dev PRs are up. thanks all.
